surprises.description: Euronet cut its 2026 outlook rather than reaffirming the prior 10–15% adjusted EPS growth range: it now expects roughly 10% growth, with revenue of about $4.375 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $725 million. Management cited persistent cross-border pressure from U.S. immigration policy and macro weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “cut its full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $4.375 billion in revenue, $725 million in adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS growth of roughly 10%,” citing “persistent cross-border headwinds from US immigration policy and macro weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EPS: Guidance: +10–15% → $10.57–$11.05”; “FY2026 revenue: Guidance: ~+6%”; the base case expected “FY reaffirmed at 10–15%.”

surprises.description: Cross-Border profitability deteriorated more sharply than the preview’s base expectation: operating income fell 35% and adjusted EBITDA fell 32%, rather than declining around 20%. Revenue was down 4%, while roughly $6 million of incremental advertising spend added pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cross-border payments segment saw revenue decline 4%, operating income drop 35%, and adjusted EBITDA fall 32%,” hurt by U.S. outbound pressure and “roughly $6 million in incremental advertising spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Cross-Border −4% with op income −20%”; the preview said the key metric was whether the Q2 “−34%” operating-income decline would compress toward “−10/−15%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income was well below the preview’s estimate: reported adjusted operating income was $169.9 million versus an estimated $198–205 million. The preview had highlighted segment margins as a key risk, but the consolidated shortfall was substantially larger than its modeled range.
Adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s roughly $245–252 million estimate, at $226.1 million. That missed the preview’s key threshold for a roughly flat year-over-year result.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$245–252M (derived, not published)”; the catalyst checklist flagged “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA ≥ ~$245M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS missed the published $3.69 consensus: Euronet reported $3.55, down 2% year over year instead of the roughly 2% growth implied by consensus. The result was nevertheless at the bottom of the preview’s $3.55–$3.75 base-case range and close to its cited buy-side whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $3.55, a 2% year-over-year decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $3.69”; the preview said the “effective buy-side whisper looks like $3.40–$3.55” and its base case was “$3.55–3.75.”

surprises.description: Payments Infrastructure revenue grew faster than the preview’s segment estimate, at 9% versus its projected 6–8%. However, operating income was flat, consistent with the preview’s concern that cost inflation and mix would limit profit conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payments infrastructure revenue grew 9% on merchant acquiring and CoreCard, but adjusted operating income was flat,” with global cost inflation and a $4.7 million CoreCard purchase-price amortization charge weighing on profitability.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “$434–442M” versus $409.4 million a year earlier, or “+6% to +8%”; the base case expected “Payments Infrastructure +7% with flat margins.”

surprises.description: Euronet repurchased more shares in the quarter than the preview expected for the second half: about 690,000 shares for $50 million, versus an expectation of only 400,000–500,000 shares planned for all of H2 and no additional repurchases built into guidance. The buyback had minimal immediate EPS impact but was expected to help future quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased approximately 690,000 shares for $50 million during the quarter, with minimal Q3 EPS impact but expected benefit to future quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “only 400–500k shares planned for H2” and “no incremental repurchase baked into guidance.”

surprises.description: Management indicated that 2027 adjusted EPS growth would likely be toward the lower end of the 10–15% Investor Day framework, pointing to a weaker starting point from persistent cross-border weakness. The preview discussed that framework but did not anticipate this lower-end outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management signaled 2027 adjusted EPS growth likely toward the lower end of its 10-15% Investor Day framework, reflecting a partial rebasing from persistent cross-border weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referenced the “23% Investor Day framework” for digital accelerators, but did not flag a lower-end 2027 EPS outlook; it described the 10–15% range as a framework.

surprises.description: A new epay headwind emerged: Steam will stop selling physical gift cards at the end of October, creating a Q4 gap. The expected gradual offset from the mid-November Grand Theft Auto 6 release does not eliminate that near-term headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Steam will discontinue physical gift card sales at the end of October, creating a Q4 headwind for epay,” while the GTA 6 release is “expected to gradually offset the gap.”
